page: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8175M processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tasks, fall into the bottom 25% of tested servers. However, multi-core performance, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, reaches average levels. Notably, the instance demonstrates strong read-only memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks, though write bandwidth and small-block read bandwidth remain average.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage its 64 vCPUs, such as database operations, static web serving, and software compilation, which all register average benchmark scores. It is less suited for single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM text generation due to weak performance in those areas. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile offers a standard general-purpose resource density, but the trade-off lies in its lower single-core efficiency compared to its multi-core capacity.
